To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a new approach to meta-learning which can be trained on a distribution of tasks without requiring the data to be segmented into tasks.
we propose a new meta-learning framework that allows learning in the absence of task segmentation and demonstrate the utility of our approach on a variety of tasks.
we introduce MOCA, a meta-learning algorithm that can be trained and tested on a single time series without segmentation into tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing meta-learning algorithms which can be applied in settings where tasks are unknown, and data is collected continuously and online.
the problem of continual learning in a meta-learning setting.
the following question: can meta-learning be used to learn in the presence of a time-vary task?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOCA is an interesting approach for meta-learning that can be applied in settings where the data is not segmented according to tasks, and can outperform baselines in these settings.
MOCA is a promising approach for enabling meta-learning algorithms in settings where task segmentation is unavailable.

the proposed MOCA framework enables the application of meta-learning to settings where task segmentation is unavailable and allows for continual meta-learning without tasks, while maintaining a strong performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MOCA is a generic meta-learning approach that can be applied to any task where data is available as a stream of time series.
we show how meta-learning can work in a more realistic setting, where tasks are not pre-segmented.
MOCA can be applied to both offline and online learning, and can be used for both regression and classification tasks, and is a general framework for continual meta-learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meta-learning can be applied in the absence of task segmentation, enabling its use in a wider range of applications.
the MOCA framework enables the application of meta-learning algorithms to a wide range of settings that have previously not been accessible.
